content.text:
I have a complete picture. Here is my report.

## Editing surface technology

The editor is **TipTap** (a wrapper over **ProseMirror**), instantiated directly via `new Editor({...})` from `@tiptap/core` — not the React/Qwik binding. The host UI framework is **Qwik** (`component$`, `useStore`, `useVisibleTask$`, `$`).

- Editor component: `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx` (3254 lines) — this is where all the real work lives.
- Route: `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/routes/editor/index.tsx` (1079 lines) — a layout shell that mounts `<TwyneEditor>` plus side panels (`PersonasPanel`, `RubricPanel`, `CommentsPanel`, `CitationsPanel`) and wires the `twyne:*` custom-event bus.

The editing surface is the ProseMirror contenteditable, mounted in `useVisibleTask$` around line 398–441: `import("@tiptap/core").then(({ Editor }) => { const editor = new Editor({ element: el, extensions: [...], editorProps: { attributes: { class: "ProseMirror" } } }) })`. The extension list (lines 443–482) includes `StarterKit`, tables, and the custom marks `CommentMark`, `PersonaNoteMark`, `SuggestionMark`, plus `EndnoteNode` and `MermaidDiagram`.

## How comments/notes are anchored to text

Comments and notes are **TipTap marks**, so they serialize into the saved folio HTML and travel with the text (no separate offset store).

- Persona/editor margin notes: `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/editor/extensions/persona-note-mark.ts` — `PersonaNoteMark`, rendered as `<span class="twyne-persona-note" data-persona-note-id/author/color/label/note/quote/brief ...>`. Anchored by `onPersonaNotes` (twyne-editor.tsx ~914): it takes each note's `quote`, calls `findTextRange(editor.state.doc, n.quote)` to locate the passage, and applies the mark over that range.
- Writer's own inline comments: `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/editor/extensions/comment-mark.ts` — `CommentMark`, rendered as `<span class="twyne-comment-mark" data-comment-id ...>` with a `cursor: pointer` inline style and mustard underline.
- Editor rewrite proposals: `SuggestionMark` (`.twyne-suggestion`).

Because they are marks, the popover code re-derives geometry from the live DOM span via `getBoundingClientRect()` rather than storing coordinates.

## The hover interaction (trigger, positioning, conflict)

All three are handled by **delegated native DOM listeners attached to the editor element `el`** (not TipTap plugins, not CSS `:hover`). This is the crux of the editing conflict.

Trigger (twyne-editor.tsx ~723):
```js
// ── Hover: preview a persona note below its sentence ──
el.addEventListener("mouseover", (e) => {
  const noteSpan = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest(".twyne-persona-note");
  if (!noteSpan) return;
  if (store.notePopover?.pinned) return;   // don't clobber a pinned card
  buildAndPin(noteSpan, false);            // pinned=false → hover-preview
});
el.addEventListener("mouseout", (e) => {
  if (store.notePopover?.pinned) return;
  if (store.notePopover?.replying) return;                 // stay open mid-reply
  if ((store.notePopover?.thread.length ?? 0) > 0) return; // stay open if thread exists
  const related = e.relatedTarget as HTMLElement | null;
  if (related?.closest(".persona-note-card")) return;      // moving onto the card
  if (related?.closest(".twyne-persona-note")) return;
  store.notePopover = null;
});
```

Positioning: `buildNotePopover` (~659) and the pure, unit-tested `computePopoverGeometry` in `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/editor/popover-positioning.ts`. Card is 340px wide, `max-height: min(60vh, 520px)`; it prefers to sit just below the marked span (`rect.bottom + 8`), and when that would clip the viewport bottom it **shifts up to overlap the sentence** (a deliberate choice — the comment quotes it as keeping the card "reachable on hover"). The card is `position: fixed; z-50` (JSX at line 2580–2606).

Why hover conflicts with editing:
1. **The popover deliberately overlaps the text it's anchored to.** The positioning logic shifts the fixed, `z-50` card up over the sentence rather than leaving a gap, so it literally covers the passage the writer would click into to edit.
2. **Hover fires from `mouseover` on the whole editor surface**, so simply moving the mouse across a marked sentence while editing spawns the card. There is no hover-intent delay/debounce and no "suppress while typing" guard — the only guards are `pinned`, `replying`, and `thread.length > 0`.
3. **The card steals the click target.** Because it's `z-50` and overlaps, clicking to place the caret in a marked passage can land on the card instead of the text. The `.twyne-comment-mark` span also carries `cursor: pointer`, and a single click on it is intercepted by the click handler (see below) to open the margin popover rather than placing a caret.

## Click handling and the "strike down" / dismiss mechanism

Click delegation (~747):
```js
el.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
  const commentMark = target.closest(".twyne-comment-mark");
  if (commentMark) { openUserCommentPopover(commentId, commentMark); return; } // pins margin card
  // ...suggestion span → suggestionPopover...
  const noteSpan = target.closest(".twyne-persona-note");
  if (noteSpan) buildAndPin(noteSpan, true);           // click PINS the note card open
  else if (!target.closest(".persona-note-card")) store.notePopover = null; // click-away closes
});
```

Dismissal paths:
- **Strike** button (JSX ~2813): the primary "strike down" action inside the note card. `onClick$` calls `dismissNote(store.notePopover.id)` then `store.notePopover = null`. `dismissNote` (~1214) is `removePersonaNote(store.editor, id)` — it **removes the mark from the document** and clears the popover.
- **✕ close button** (~2637) and clicking anywhere outside the card: just `store.notePopover = null` (hides card, keeps the mark).
- **Click-away**: the click handler sets `notePopover = null` when the target is neither a note span nor `.persona-note-card`; a top-level `mousedown` handler (~377) also dismisses layout/table popovers on outside click.
- **Double-click escape hatch** (~814) — this is the current workaround for the editing conflict on writer comments:
```js
el.addEventListener("dblclick", (e) => {
  const commentMark = target.closest(".twyne-comment-mark");
  if (!commentMark) return;
  store.userCommentPopover = null;                       // dismiss the popover
  const pos = editor.view.posAtDOM(commentMark, 0);      // resolve mark → PM position
  if (typeof pos === "number" && pos >= 0) editor.commands.focus(pos); // caret into passage
  else editor.commands.focus();
});
```
So today, to edit inside a commented passage the writer must double-click to punch through the pinned popover and drop the caret in.
- **Escape**: `if (e.key === "Escape")` handlers exist only on individual reply/input textareas (lines 2292, 2346, 2399, 2451, 2777) — there is **no global Escape handler that closes `notePopover`**.
- Writer comments can also be **resolved** (not removed) via `toggleUserCommentResolved` (imported line 39; used ~1376) — resolution is stored in `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/user-comments.ts`, separate from the mark.

## State machinery governing interaction modes

State lives in a Qwik `useStore<EditorStore>` inside `TwyneEditor` (initialized ~250). The interaction-mode-relevant fields (interface at lines 82–166):

- `notePopover: NotePopover | null` — the persona/editor note card. Its `pinned`, `replying`, `thread`, `dismissed`, `draft`, and `error` fields form the de-facto state machine for hover-vs-click-vs-conversation. `pinned` is the key flag: hover sets it false (auto-dismiss on mouseout), click sets it true (survives mouseout).
- `userCommentPopover: UserCommentPopover | null` — the writer's own inline-comment margin card (`resolved`, `replies`, `draft`).
- `suggestionPopover: SuggestionPopover | null` — editor rewrite accept/strike card.
- `zenMode: boolean` — the closest thing to a "focus/view mode." When on, CSS (`.twyne-editor.zen-mode`, styles at lines 274–316) dims/quiets `.twyne-persona-note`, `.twyne-comment-mark`, citations, endnotes, and the toolbar/header/footer (they reappear on `:hover`). Toggling dispatches `twyne:zen-mode`; the **route** (`/routes/editor/index.tsx` ~330, `zenModeHandler`) collapses side panels and restores them via `panelsBeforeZen`. Note: zen mode dims the marks visually but does **not** disable the hover/click popover listeners — the conflict persists in zen mode.
- There is **no `editable`/`readonly` flag** passed to the TipTap `Editor` — the surface is always editable; the only "modes" are `zenMode` and the presence/pinned-state of the popovers.

Route-level layout state (`LayoutStore` in index.tsx ~150): `rightPanel: "personas" | "rubric" | "comments" | "citations"`, `rightPanelOpen`, `panelsBeforeZen`, `zenMode`, `rightPanelWidth`.

## The persona-reply event flow (as you noted)

Comments and notes are **TipTap marks**, so they serialize into the saved folio HTML and travel with the text (no separate offset store).

1. **The popover deliberately overlaps the text it's anchored to.** The positioning logic shifts the fixed, `z-50` card up over the sentence rather than leaving a gap, so it literally covers the passage the writer would click into to edit.

Hovering inline comments/persona notes in the TipTap editor conflicts with editing: the note card deliberately shifts up **over** the anchored sentence when near the viewport bottom, hover fires instantly with no intent delay or typing suppression, and a single click on a marked span is intercepted to open the popover instead of placing the caret (the only escape hatch is a hidden dblclick handler). The user rejected "modes"; the approved design makes the popover **non-blocking**: never covers the text, never steals the caret click, never appears while typing.

- `twyne-editor.tsx` does **not** use the pure `computePopoverGeometry` module — `buildNotePopover` duplicates the math inline. The module + its tests are currently dead code; this plan makes the editor consume it.

## Changes

Replace "shift up over the sentence" with prefer-below / flip-above:

Clamp `maxH` to available space so the card shrinks instead of overlapping.
- Update `popover-positioning.test.ts`: rewrite the "shifts up" and tiny-viewport tests to assert flip-above + `bottom`/`maxH`; add a shrink-below case; x-clamp tests just gain a `top` field.
